newsitem.title: USA: Chubb favors internal growth over acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Chubb favors internal growth over acquisitions.

text.p: ATLANTA, April 15, Reuter - Chubb Corp plans to further expand its operations outside the United States, but would prefer to generate that growth internally rather than through acquisitions, a top Chubb executive said.

"If you ask me are we going to make any major overseas acquisitions, I guess I would say if something came along that really did something for us, we'd do it," Chubb Chief Executive Dean O'Hare told Reuters in an interview at the 35th annual Risk and Insurance Management conference here.
However, O'Hare said as a specialty property-casualty company, Chubb would only be interested in companies that brought new and different to Chubb.
"Adding a few hundred million dollars in premiums, or even a billion dollars in premiums, you're talking about one year's growth," O'Hare said.
"So, why would you want to make an acquisition with all the uncertainties connected with an acquisition, because there are plenty of uncertainties," he said.
"I don't want to close the door on acquisitions, but it clearly would not be at the top of my priorities unless we really found something that was different and exciting," he said.
Chubb's sale of its life insurance business earlier this year for $875 million prompted speculation that the company might use at least some of the proceeds for international acquisitions.
The company has previously said it intends to use the proceeds for a stock buyback.
O'Hare said the buyback will boost the company's overall return on equity to at least 15 percent by next year.
Chubb, which already has a formidable presence in property- casualty markets outside the United States, plans to push for additional growth in India and China, O'Hare said.
"There are other places we are looking at and it is very early stages of getting involved in and that would be Poland and Indonesia," he said.
But, O'Hare said, he believes the overseas specialty lines offers the best opportunities for growth.
"I think there are greater opportunities in the specialty lines overseas than here in the United States," he said.
